To secure an economy of autonomous agents against Sybil attacks without relying on human biometrics, networks implement cryptoeconomic staking bounded by a strict slashing horizon. When an agent registers, it must lock collateral
 into a designated smart contract. If malicious coordination or fake-identity flooding threatens the consensus, validation metrics will spiral downward, triggering automated proofs of identity fraud. The protocol then confiscates the staked assets, rendering the attacker's capital hollow and economically irrational.
